title: Credit buckets shortfall redistribution & billing rules PRD
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement: Enterprise customers on multi-product contracts often hit a quota shortfall in one product while holding unused credits in another. Current behavior is to block calls or bill immediate overage at list rates, which causes unexpected outages and invoice disputes. This PRD defines entitlement-driven shortfall redistribution (moving credit from sibling buckets within the same contract), a configurable grace window, and deterministic billing rules for proration and overage accounting. Goals: 1) Reduce customer-facing outages due to single-bucket depletion. 2) Reduce invoice disputes by making redistribution and billing predictable and auditable. 3) Preserve accounting correctness and compliance across regions. Scope: - Design entitlement rules for eligible buckets (same-customer, same-billing-account, optional permission flag on plans). - Runtime behavior for automatic redistribution vs. soft-decline with prompt to buyer. - Billing logic for proration when redistribution occurs mid-cycle. - Admin controls in Console to opt-out, cap redistribution, or force strict isolation. Out of scope: cross-currency automatic conversions between international billing ledgers (will require finance sign-off in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Metering: When a request would exceed primary bucket, the runtime must attempt redistribution from eligible sibling buckets within 200ms before returning a quota response.
Eligibility: Redistribution must only occur if sibling buckets have entitlements marked 'redistributable' and belong to the same billing account and currency.

Grace window: For plans with 'auto-redistribute' enabled, allow a configurable grace window (default 6 minutes) where temporary negative balances in the primary bucket are permitted while redistribution completes; outside that window requests are soft-declined.

Billing: Any tokens or usage moved via redistribution must be recorded as an internal transfer line item on the invoice with origin_bucket_id, dest_bucket_id, transfer_amount, transfer_timestamp, and transfer_reason.

Proration: When redistribution causes consumption to cross a plan boundary (e.g., from trial to paid or from monthly to annual allocations), billing should prorate at the effective time and expose prorated adjustment lines on the next invoice.

Overage pricing: If redistribution is not possible or disabled, overage charges apply at plan-specific overage rates and appear on the next invoice; system must support either per-token or per-request overage meters depending on plan configuration.

Auditability: Console must show a transfer history panel with filters for date, billing account, and transfer_reason. Each transfer must link to the originating request IDs or aggregated request ranges.
Rollback: Admin API must be able to reverse a redistribution transfer within 72 hours, generating a reversing invoice adjustment line and an audit record.
Edge behavior: If sibling buckets are in different currencies, redistribution must be denied and a clear error code returned to calling SDKs (no silent conversions).

Tests: Integration test coverage for redistribution success/failure, performance measured (p95 latency for a redistribution decision < 250ms), and end-to-end billing reconciliation tests comparing expected invoice lines with simulated usage.
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff with Billing, Finance, and Runtime teams. Agreed to prefer explicit 'redistributable' flag on plan entitlements to avoid unintended transfers.
2026-02-23: Design review — runtime will query entitlement metadata service at evaluation time; ENG raised concern about extra latency — agreed to cache entitlement flags for 5 minutes at edge.
2026-03-02: Finance approved invoice presentation and required ledger fields; asked to include transfer_reason codes for reconciliation (CODE_PROMO, CODE_MANUAL_ADJ, CODE_AUTOMATIC_REDISTRIBUTE).
2026-03-08: Security reviewed sensitive fields; KMS encryption required for transfer line item IDs stored in reporting DB.
2026-03-10: PM updated acceptance criteria to include admin rollback and auditability requirements after legal feedback on customer disputes.
implementation_notes: Runtime will implement a two-step flow: 1) fast local evaluation against cached entitlements; 2) background confirmation with canonical entitlement service for final billing attribution. Billing engine will accept transfer webhook events and persist transfer lines. Must add idempotency keys to transfer events to avoid double-billing. Planned implementation tasks: ENG-3284 (runtime decision path), ENG-3310 (transfer event schema + ingestion), ENG-3333 (console transfer history UI).
open_questions: Should redistribution be allowed across product families (e.g., embeddings <-> generation) if explicit mapping exists?
What is the default cap per redistribution event (absolute tokens or percentage of donor bucket)? Finance recommends limiting to 25% per event for high-value accounts.
How do we present redistribution to end-users in usage emails and webhooks to minimize confusion?
edge_cases: Simultaneous depletion race: two concurrent requests exhausting donor bucket — runtime must use atomic transfer reservation or fail-safe to avoid double-transfer.
Chargeback disputes: customer claims a transfer was unexpected — need exportable CSV of transfers with request IDs and timestamps.
Plan migration mid-cycle: user upgrades plan during redistribution -> ensure proration and transfer attribution are tied to the timestamped entitlement state.
next_steps: ENG to submit RFC for entitlement caching and transfer idempotency by 2026-03-17 (ENG-3284).
Finance to publish final transfer_reason code list and reconciliation mapping by 2026-03-20.
Design to add transfer history UI mocks for Console review by 2026-03-22 (DES-2145).
PM to schedule pilot with two enterprise customers for April billing cycle; collect dispute and UX metrics.
